summary: Idaho County 40-foot pole tower with an L-6 cab, built in 1931 in the Nez Perce National Forest and destroyed in 1968; no source describes what remains.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with an L-6 cab and an accompanying cabin for living quarters
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1968; no source describes what remains at the site.

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists the site as hike-in; no source describes a trail or current access.

events.note: 40-foot pole tower with L-6 cab and cabin living quarters

evidence.supports: built 1931 as a 40-foot pole L-6 tower with accompanying cabin
evidence.quote: This 40' pole L-6 tower and accompanying cabin living quarters, built in 1931, were destroyed

evidence.supports: located 11 miles southwest of Elk City, Idaho
evidence.quote: Located 11 miles southwest of Elk City, Idaho.

evidence.supports: photographs courtesy The Fire Lookout Museum

sources.title: Nipple Mountain Lookout
sources.publisher: Idaho Cities and Towns Collection, University of Idaho Library

notes_for_editor: firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts agree on 1931 build and 1968 destruction; the UI Cities and Towns record confirms the Elk City location only and is not dated. The FFLA list says gone. The Idaho page's 1931 and 1968 lines use en dashes and a prime symbol; only the matching lines were quoted. Search snippets showed UI photos dated 1932-1933 showing a cabin and tower; these are photo dates, not read, not used. No staffing or fire history found. Photo already on the record; no new photo added.
